description: A classic American exterior front entry photographed in autumn light. The house facade is white-painted brick with crisp dark-framed multi-pane windows and grey-green wooden shutters. The focal point is a grand arched doorway framed by a painted plaster surround — a Roman arch with a graceful fanlight transom window above a raised-panel front door in a warm greige-taupe tone. The door has a traditional divided-light sidelight on the right and a matte-black lever handle with smart lock hardware. A wide landing of light limestone or concrete steps with a substantial stone coping leads up to the door, flanked by stone or cement planters holding lush spreading ferns on the left and a compact silvery-leafed shrub on the right. Low boxwood hedges and an established Japanese maple with burnt-orange autumn foliage frame the left side of the composition, while trimmed globe shrubs anchor the right. The front walk is pale natural stone pavers, slightly receding toward the frame's bottom. The overall atmosphere is elegant, autumnal, and traditionally symmetrical. Natural soft autumn daylight bathes the scene evenly, with warm tones in the foliage providing the only color punctuation. Camera is at standing eye-level, level pitch, with a normal lens in a centered symmetrical composition showing the full entry facade.
